+//! Setup-only native Classic Cut 2S records, from Quintin Smits's MIT Agie Processor and our offline control checks.
+//!
+//! This encoder references an existing ISO geometry file for one closed punch.
+//! The caller must verify the nominal contour, its lead from the threading hole,
+//! and the compensated cuts against the stock, installed travel and fixtures.
+//! The piece uses stock top Z0, 20 mm steel 0001, Berco Cut 0.25 and a 1 mm separation.
+//!
+//! Place the SBL script and SBR resource manifest beside the ISO, with the same
+//! stem and their respective extensions. Import the ISO geometry into ISO Sys.
+//! Keep the matching SBR beside the SBL when importing the script into SBL Sys.
+//! Create a new workpiece from the imported script. Earlier pieces can retain
+//! their erosion steps on repeat import. In the new piece, match the work's ISO
+//! geometry and start hole to the setup and confirm zero steps. Follow
+//! [`SetupFiles::controller_review`] before assigning TECCUT.
+//!
+//! ```
+//! use camcraft_post::agie_setup::PunchSetup20;
+//!
+//! let setup = PunchSetup20 {
+//!     stem: "CCSEP20",
+//!     stock_min_um: [-40_000, -30_000],
+//!     stock_max_um: [40_000, 30_000],
+//!     start_hole_um: [-30_000, 0],
+//! };
+//! let files = setup.encode()?;
+//! assert_eq!(files.sbr, "AGIE.USING_CCSEP20.ISO IMPORT CCSEP20.ISO;\r\n");
+//! assert!(files.sbl.contains("ASDELETE"));
+//! # Ok::<(), camcraft_post::agie_setup::SetupError>(())
+//! ```
+
+/// Setup coordinates for a closed punch with a predrilled 2 mm start hole.
+/// XY coordinates are integer micrometres in the same work frame as the ISO.
+#[derive(Debug)]
+pub struct PunchSetup20<'a> {
+    /// Common DOS file stem for the ISO, SBR and SBL (for example, `CCSEP20`).
+    pub stem: &'a str,
+    /// Lower stock limits [X, Y].
+    pub stock_min_um: [i32; 2],
+    /// Upper stock limits [X, Y].
+    pub stock_max_um: [i32; 2],
+    /// Centre of the threading hole [X, Y].
+    pub start_hole_um: [i32; 2],
+}
+
+/// The two native setup files. Save their ASCII bytes with the supplied CRLF endings.
+#[derive(Debug)]
+pub struct SetupFiles {
+    /// Piece script for the control.
+    pub sbl: String,
+    /// Import manifest referring to the caller's ISO geometry.
+    pub sbr: String,
+    /// Operator checks for the installed effective work technology.
+    pub controller_review: &'static str,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
+pub enum SetupError {
+    #[error(
+        "Use a DOS stem of 1 to 8 uppercase letters or digits beginning with a letter. Choose a name other than a DOS device."
+    )]
+    InvalidStem,
+    #[error(
+        "Use increasing stock bounds. The stock and work origin must fit the 350 × 250 mm XY span."
+    )]
+    InvalidStock,
+    #[error("Place the complete 2 mm start hole inside the stock.")]
+    HoleOutsideStock,
+}
+
+impl PunchSetup20<'_> {
+    /// Encode one native work with zero erosion steps on import.
+    ///
+    /// # Errors
+    /// Refuses invalid file stems, stock bounds and threading-hole positions.
+    pub fn encode(&self) -> Result<SetupFiles, SetupError> {
+        if !valid_stem(self.stem) {
+            return Err(SetupError::InvalidStem);
+        }
+        for (axis, stroke_um) in [350_000, 250_000].into_iter().enumerate() {
+            let min = i64::from(self.stock_min_um[axis]);
+            let max = i64::from(self.stock_max_um[axis]);
+            let hole = i64::from(self.start_hole_um[axis]);
+            if min >= max || max.max(0) - min.min(0) > stroke_um {
+                return Err(SetupError::InvalidStock);
+            }
+            if hole - 1000 < min || hole + 1000 > max {
+                return Err(SetupError::HoleOutsideStock);
+            }
+        }
+        Ok(SetupFiles {
+            sbl: piece(self),
+            sbr: format!("AGIE.USING_{0}.ISO IMPORT {0}.ISO;\r\n", self.stem),
+            controller_review: concat!(
+                "Import the ISO into ISO Sys and keep its SBR beside the SBL during script import. ",
+                "Select the newly created piece. Earlier pieces can retain their steps on repeat import. ",
+                "Match this work's ISO resource, geometry and start hole to the setup. Confirm zero steps. ",
+                "Verify steel 0001, Berco Cut 0.25 and 20 mm. CCB030 requests Ra 0.30, Te 1.50, ",
+                "Tkm 1.00 and three disabled options. Check the effective values and both visible options ",
+                "on this work. Assign the matching TECCUT row. Check offsets of 245, 155, 140 and ",
+                "134 µm in order before GRAFICHECK and FORMALCHECK.",
+            ),
+        })
+    }
+}
+
+/// Whether the stem can name the matching ISO, SBR and SBL on Agie Control.
+pub fn valid_stem(stem: &str) -> bool {
+    let bytes = stem.as_bytes();
+    (1..=8).contains(&bytes.len())
+        && bytes[0].is_ascii_uppercase()
+        && bytes
+            .iter()
+            .all(|c| c.is_ascii_uppercase() || c.is_ascii_digit())
+        && !matches!(stem, "CON" | "AUX" | "NUL" | "PRN")
+        && !(bytes.len() == 4
+            && (stem.starts_with("COM") || stem.starts_with("LPT"))
+            && bytes[3].is_ascii_digit())
+}
+
+/// Format native millimetres without rounding a floating point coordinate.
+fn mm(value_um: i64) -> String {
+    let sign = if value_um < 0 { "-" } else { "" };
+    let value = value_um.unsigned_abs();
+    format!("{sign}{}.{:03}", value / 1000, value % 1000)
+}
+
+fn attribute(lines: &mut Vec<String>, object: &str, context: &str, key: &str, value: &str) {
+    lines.push(format!(
+        "  ok=JE_AttribObject({object},SETATTR,je_piece,{context},{key},{value},je_dim)"
+    ));
+}
+
+fn checked(lines: &mut Vec<String>, command: String) {
+    lines.push(command);
+    lines.extend([
+        "  if (ok<>0) then".into(),
+        "    stop".into(),
+        "  end if".into(),
+    ]);
+}
+
+fn piece(setup: &PunchSetup20<'_>) -> String {
+    let [xmin, ymin] = setup.stock_min_um.map(i64::from);
+    let [xmax, ymax] = setup.stock_max_um.map(i64::from);
+    let stem = setup.stem;
+    let group = format!("\"{stem}\"");
+    let work = format!("{group},\"CUT1\"");
+    let work_context = format!("{work},NULL");
+    let hole_context = format!("{work},\"stp1\"");
+    let mut lines = vec!["'$Include \"jescript.sbh\"".into(), "sub SetOrigin".into()];
+    for (field, value) in [
+        ("ID_HEIGHT", "20.000".into()),
+        ("ID_NOMEOBJ", stem.into()),
+        ("ID_MATERIAL", "0001".into()),
+        ("ID_THREAD", "Berco Cut 0.25".into()),
+        ("ID_POSX", "0".into()),
+        ("ID_POSY", "0".into()),
+        ("ID_POSZ", "0".into()),
+        ("ID_ROTATION", "0".into()),
+        ("ID_DIML", mm(xmax - xmin)),
+        ("ID_DIMB", mm(ymax - ymin)),
+        ("ID_POSPOSX", mm(xmin)),
+        ("ID_POSPOSY", mm(ymin)),
+        ("ID_POSPOSZ", "-20.000".into()),
+        ("ID_VALSECP", "3.0".into()),
+        ("ID_VALRETP", "30.0".into()),
+    ] {
+        attribute(
+            &mut lines,
+            "PIECE",
+            "NULL,NULL,NULL",
+            field,
+            &format!("\"{value}\""),
+        );
+    }
+    lines.extend([
+        "  ok=JE_GenerateAttrib(c_tecauto,c_tecauto_t)".into(),
+        "  ok=JE_GenerateAttrib(c_tecassign,c_tecass_fi)".into(),
+        "  ok=JE_GenerateAttrib(c_tecalert,c_tecalert_sea)".into(),
+        "end sub".into(),
+        "sub CutPunch".into(),
+    ]);
+    checked(
+        &mut lines,
+        "  ok=JE_CreateQuality(je_piece,\"CCB030\",\"0.30,1.50,1.00,F,F,F\",je_q1)".into(),
+    );
+    checked(
+        &mut lines,
+        format!("  ok=JE_Create(GROUP,je_piece,{group},NULL)"),
+    );
+    checked(&mut lines, format!("  ok=JE_Create(WORK,je_piece,{work})"));
+    attribute(
+        &mut lines,
+        "WORK",
+        &work_context,
+        "ID_GEOMETRY",
+        &format!("\"AGIE.USING_{stem}.ISO\""),
+    );
+    attribute(&mut lines, "WORK", &work_context, "ID_PUNCH", "c_punch");
+    attribute(&mut lines, "WORK", &work_context, "ID_WORKCOND", "\"2\"");
+    checked(
+        &mut lines,
+        format!(
+            "  ok=JE_AttribObject(WORK,SETATTR,je_piece,{work_context},ID_QUALITY,je_q1,je_dim)"
+        ),
+    );
+    for (field, value) in [
+        ("ID_THREAD", "\"Berco Cut 0.25\""),
+        ("ID_ENTRYMODE", "c_entper"),
+        ("ID_HEIGHT", "\"20.000\""),
+        ("ID_POSX", "\"0\""),
+        ("ID_POSY", "\"0\""),
+        ("ID_SEPCUT", "\"1.0\""),
+        ("ID_REVCUT", "\"T\""),
+        ("ID_COMMPOINTENTRY", "\"3.0\""),
+        ("ID_COMMPOINTEXIT", "\"0\""),
+        ("ID_PRIORITY", "\"10\""),
+        ("ID_RADIUSMINLA", "\"T\""),
+        ("ID_I_TYPE", "c_radius_rm"),
+        ("ID_E_TYPE", "c_radius_rm"),
+        ("ID_ENTRY", "\"2\""),
+    ] {
+        attribute(&mut lines, "WORK", &work_context, field, value);
+    }
+    lines.push(format!(
+        "  ok=JE_CreateStartPoint(WORK,\"stp1\",je_piece,{work})"
+    ));
+    for (field, coordinate) in ["ID_POSX", "ID_POSY"].into_iter().zip(setup.start_hole_um) {
+        attribute(
+            &mut lines,
+            "STARTPOINT",
+            &hole_context,
+            field,
+            &format!("\"{}\"", mm(i64::from(coordinate))),
+        );
+    }
+    attribute(&mut lines, "WORK", &work_context, "ID_STP", "\"stp1\"");
+    attribute(&mut lines, "WORK", &work_context, "ID_STPMODE", "c_work");
+    attribute(
+        &mut lines,
+        "STARTPOINT",
+        &hole_context,
+        "ID_STP_PL",
+        "\"4\"",
+    );
+    attribute(
+        &mut lines,
+        "STARTPOINT",
+        &hole_context,
+        "ID_DIAMETER",
+        "\"2.0\"",
+    );
+    // An existing quality name can bind to stale data even after a successful assignment.
+    checked(
+        &mut lines,
+        format!("  ok=JE_GenerateCuts(WORK,je_piece,{work},ASDELETE,NULL)"),
+    );
+    lines.extend([
+        "end sub".into(),
+        "sub main".into(),
+        "  ok=JE_Initiate".into(),
+        "  if (ok=0) then".into(),
+        "    SetOrigin".into(),
+        "    CutPunch".into(),
+        "    ok=JE_AttribObject(PIECE,SETATTR,je_piece,je_grp,NULL,NULL,ID_STATEGY,\"EW\",je_dim)"
+            .into(),
+        "    ok=JE_ClosePiece(je_piece)".into(),
+        "  else".into(),
+        "    stop".into(),
+        "  end if".into(),
+        "end sub".into(),
+        String::new(),
+    ]);
+    lines.join("\r\n")
+}

+//! Setup-only Classic Cut 2S reference records from CamCraft's offline controller-checked synthetic punch.
+//! Gate map: covers camcraft_post::agie_setup.
+use camcraft_post::agie_setup::{PunchSetup20, SetupError};
+
+fn punch() -> PunchSetup20<'static> {
+    PunchSetup20 {
+        stem: "CCSEP20",
+        stock_min_um: [-40_000, -30_000],
+        stock_max_um: [40_000, 30_000],
+        start_hole_um: [-30_000, 0],
+    }
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn setup_files_match_the_control_checked_zero_step_punch() {
+    let files = punch().encode().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(
+        files.sbl.as_bytes(),
+        include_bytes!("golden/agie-setup/CCSEP20.SBL")
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        files.sbr.as_bytes(),
+        include_bytes!("golden/agie-setup/CCSEP20.SBR")
+    );
+    let cuts: Vec<_> = files
+        .sbl
+        .lines()
+        .filter(|l| l.contains("JE_GenerateCuts("))
+        .collect();
+    assert_eq!(
+        cuts,
+        ["  ok=JE_GenerateCuts(WORK,je_piece,\"CCSEP20\",\"CUT1\",ASDELETE,NULL)"]
+    );
+    assert!(files.controller_review.contains("245, 155, 140 and 134 µm"));
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn a_named_resource_and_signed_micron_coordinates_round_trip() {
+    let setup = PunchSetup20 {
+        stem: "DEMO2026",
+        stock_min_um: [-2_010, -1_001],
+        stock_max_um: [1_001, 1_000],
+        start_hole_um: [-1, -1],
+    };
+    let files = setup.encode().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(
+        files.sbr,
+        "AGIE.USING_DEMO2026.ISO IMPORT DEMO2026.ISO;\r\n"
+    );
+    for field in [
+        "ID_NOMEOBJ,\"DEMO2026\",je_dim",
+        "ID_GEOMETRY,\"AGIE.USING_DEMO2026.ISO\",je_dim",
+        "ID_DIML,\"3.011\",je_dim",
+        "ID_DIMB,\"2.001\",je_dim",
+        "ID_POSPOSY,\"-1.001\",je_dim",
+        "\"stp1\",ID_POSX,\"-0.001\",je_dim",
+    ] {
+        assert!(files.sbl.contains(field), "{field}");
+    }
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn device_names_paths_and_script_text_cannot_enter_an_agie_record() {
+    for stem in [
+        "",
+        "9PART",
+        "ABCDEFGHI",
+        "con",
+        "CON",
+        "COM1",
+        "LPT9",
+        "../ISO",
+        "X.ISO",
+        "X\"\r\n",
+        "Aé",
+    ] {
+        let setup = PunchSetup20 { stem, ..punch() };
+        assert_eq!(
+            setup.encode().unwrap_err(),
+            SetupError::InvalidStem,
+            "{stem:?}"
+        );
+    }
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn stock_and_full_start_hole_must_fit_the_setup_span() {
+    let setup = PunchSetup20 {
+        stock_min_um: [-175_000, -125_000],
+        stock_max_um: [175_000, 125_000],
+        start_hole_um: [174_000, -124_000],
+        ..punch()
+    };
+    assert!(setup.encode().is_ok());
+    for (min, max, hole, error) in [
+        (
+            [-175_001, -125_000],
+            [175_000, 125_000],
+            [0, 0],
+            SetupError::InvalidStock,
+        ),
+        (
+            [-175_000, -125_001],
+            [175_000, 125_000],
+            [0, 0],
+            SetupError::InvalidStock,
+        ),
+        ([0, 0], [0, 2_000], [0, 1_000], SetupError::InvalidStock),
+        (
+            [349_000, 0],
+            [351_000, 2_000],
+            [350_000, 1_000],
+            SetupError::InvalidStock,
+        ),
+        (
+            [i32::MIN, 0],
+            [i32::MAX, 10_000],
+            [0, 5_000],
+            SetupError::InvalidStock,
+        ),
+        (
+            setup.stock_min_um,
+            setup.stock_max_um,
+            [174_001, 0],
+            SetupError::HoleOutsideStock,
+        ),
+        (
+            setup.stock_min_um,
+            setup.stock_max_um,
+            [0, -124_001],
+            SetupError::HoleOutsideStock,
+        ),
+        (
+            setup.stock_min_um,
+            setup.stock_max_um,
+            [i32::MAX, 0],
+            SetupError::HoleOutsideStock,
+        ),
+    ] {
+        let bad = PunchSetup20 {
+            stock_min_um: min,
+            stock_max_um: max,
+            start_hole_um: hole,
+            ..setup
+        };
+        assert_eq!(bad.encode().unwrap_err(), error);
+    }
+}

+## #2945 - Native Agie wire job for a rectangular punch
+
+Write the ISO geometry, SBR reference and SBL job in CamCraft. Use the existing post crate for the writer. Keep document checks and nominal geometry extraction in the app. The post crate uses tempfile for same-volume staging and rustix or windows-sys for an atomic rename that cannot replace another job. These dependencies already occur in the lockfile. No new dependency between CamCraft crates is needed. An external generator would add an installation requirement.
+
+Use the Classic 2S template from #2946. The operator adds the AGIE_QN2 condition and selects the 1 mm separation length. The template stays unconfigured until then. Use nominal geometry because the resident control determines the wire offsets and trims. Applying the preview gap to the exported contour would compensate twice.
+
+Limit the first job to one captured rectangular punch in 20 mm stock. The offline control plotted the 0.25 mm Berco wire outside the punch. Its rough centre offset was 0.245 mm. Adding the 0.125 mm wire radius and rounding outward gives a 0.4 mm stock margin. The entry needs 3 mm of straight face on either side. The control cuts the separate 1 mm interval after the long passes. Other thicknesses, conditions, profiles and separation lengths need separate control evidence before the guards change. The setup and physical release still need an operator check.
+
+Use the standalone `camcraft_post::agie_setup::PunchSetup20` encoder from #2984 for every native job. It writes a setup with zero erosion steps and returns the checks for the CLI and GUI. An existing native quality can bind to different effective settings. Remove the earlier automatic step generation. The operator must confirm the newly imported work and assign its technology. The rectangular geometry and atomic three-file publication still use the original writer.
+
+The contributor's team published the reference implementation under MIT. The notice is in `assets/ui/LICENSES.md`. The public manuals explain the file roles, object calls and quality targets. The detailed JEScript call sequence, its arguments and the QN2 inputs follow the contributor's published implementation. Some of those interface details came from observed controller examples. Whether that reference meets this project's source rules is an open review question in #2945. The PR includes no vendor runtime, controller database, firmware or vendor program. The byte goldens are CamCraft output for original synthetic geometry.
+
+- [Agie-CAM source at 11b1bb9](https://github.com/qsmits/Agie-CAM/tree/11b1bb9ef2c752b94b6fefc1f0814acd2e030c42)
+- [EZ-CAM AgieVision file workflow](https://www.ez-cam.de/downloads/v2017_edm_news.pdf)
+- [Kovoprog manual, section 3.4.1](https://www.kovoprog.cz/pictures/files/manuals/MainBook_kpd_en_open.pdf)
+- [Cimatron AgieVision quality targets](https://help.cimatron.com/en/2026/wizards/agievision/wedm_w_agv_step_5_7.htm)

+## #2946 - AGIECUT Classic 2S machine template
+
+Ship a machine library entry for setup. Section 1.1 (p. 4) gives the U and V limits relative to the vertical wire and the rapid speed for each axis. Section 5.2 (p. 44) lists electrode wires. The template includes the listed diameters within the standard Classic range of 0.20 to 0.33 mm. [AGIE technical data C2.1, June 2002](https://static.gindumac.com/products/9ccc9b7e-b589-49db-9843-eff1da09434c/documents/ES-EDM-AGI-2002-00001.pdf)
+
+Keep the X, Y and Z stroke lengths in the description. Centering them on zero would invent the endpoints in the user's setup. The taper rating depends on the guide and work height. Leave the taper limit and guide heights unset until the operator specifies the installation.
+
+The machine entry supplies no post or generator conditions. A wire operation needs a condition from the user's control before CamCraft can generate its path. An operator can save a configured copy of the template without changing the shipped file. Adding a native job writer requires separate control-specific sources and verification.

+
+Provide a Rust API that encodes the SBL piece script and its SBR import manifest for an existing nominal ISO. Use one closed punch, 20 mm steel 0001, Berco Cut 0.25 and the measured Ra 0.30 request. +

The first workspace writer must use the guarded encoder and retain its own contour, stock and lead checks. A generic post filter could miss a writer that publishes its own files. +# Post an Agie Classic Cut 2S job
+
+CamCraft writes the nominal contour, resource manifest and piece script directly. The job opens with zero erosion steps. It requests cold die steel (material 0001), Berco Cut 0.25 mm wire and a target finish of Ra 0.30 µm. Check the effective work technology on the installed control before assigning any cutting steps. The control calculates the offsets and trims. The CamCraft wire-center preview uses a 0.005 mm representative finishing gap.
+
+## Post from the Wire EDM workspace
+
+1. Mount **AGIECUT Classic 2S (template)** as the setup machine. In the machine editor, open **EDM** and add a condition with ID **AGIE_QN2**, role **rough**, wire diameter **0.25 mm** and preview gap **0.005 mm**. Apply this change to the mounted machine. Choose **Agie native wire EDM** in the post picker.
+2. Define axis-aligned rectangular stock, 20 mm thick and at most 350 × 250 mm in plan. The stock and work origin together must fit that span. Verify the installed work datum and the available axis travel on Agie Control. CamCraft refuses profiles with a stated X or Y travel limit because its preview cannot check the full resident path against that limit. Put the first, unrotated work origin on the stock top. Its XY position determines the job coordinates.
+3. Use one modeled workpiece and create one **Wire Contour** on the complete punch model. Use an axis-aligned rectangular punch with vertical sides and flat ends at the stock planes. Leave at least 0.4 mm of stock beyond each face. On the tested 20 mm QN2 job, the rough wire centre ran 0.245 mm outside the punch. The stock margin includes the 0.125 mm wire radius. Additional bodies, selected subprofiles, holes, steps and concavities are refused. Select a 0.25 mm wire and condition **AGIE_QN2**. Set the work planes to the stock top and bottom, and specify how the punch is captured. The capture setting confirms support for the punch when it is released. Keep the wire vertical. Taper, four-axis, die cuts, burnout, explicit skims, tabs and fixture models are unsupported.
+4. Place the centre of a predrilled 2 mm threading hole in the waste. The entire hole must be inside the stock. Allow a perpendicular approach to the interior of a straight outside face with at least 3 mm of lead and at least 3 mm of straight face on each side of the entry. Generate the operation.
+5. Open **Post**, choose **One program** and keep the general post settings at their defaults. Under **Agie technology**, set **Separation cut length (mm)** to **1.0**. Zero leaves the separation unspecified and blocks the post. This length applies to the separation segment that Agie Control generates. Check its position, trims and release sequence in the control’s job preview. Enter the parent folder and a fresh **Job folder name** such as `PUNCH40`. Use up to eight uppercase letters or digits, beginning with a letter. The post publishes the entire directory after validation. To retain an earlier job, give the new one a different name.
+
+## Try the synthetic punch
+
+From the project root, run the supplied script with a local CamCraft desktop CLI build.
+
+```sh
+cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/punch.camscript
+```
+
+The script imports an original 40 × 20 × 20 mm rectangular punch, places it in 80 × 60 × 20 mm stock and sets the threading point at X−30 Y0. Its post call selects the native separation with `options: {separationLengthMm: 1.0}`. Stock top is Z0 in the Agie job. The `PUNCH40` directory contains the nominal contour in `PUNCH40.ISO`, its import reference in `PUNCH40.SBR` and the piece, start point and requested quality in `PUNCH40.SBL`. Existing destinations are refused. Edit the script’s output name to make another job.
+
+## Open the job in Agie Control
+
+Keep all three files together. In the control’s file manager, open **Imp/exp** and import the ISO object into **ISO Sys**. Then import the SBL into **SBL Sys**, keeping the matching SBR beside the SBL. In the workpiece list choose **New workpiece → Script Files**, select the imported SBL and confirm with **OK**.
+
+Select the newly created piece. After a repeat import, an earlier piece can retain its machining steps. Match the new work’s ISO geometry and threading hole to the setup. Check that the new work shows **[0]**. At this point **FORMALCHECK** should report undefined technology.
+
+1. Open **Work Details** on the new work. Verify steel **0001**, wire **Berco Cut 0.25**, stock height **20 mm** and the effective work quality. The requested **CCB030** values are **Ra 0.30**, **Te 1.50** and **Tkm 1.00**, with three options disabled. Check the two options the control displays. A resident quality with the same name can hold different values.
+2. If any visible value differs, use **Quality → Define** on this work to select the requested values. Confirm the effective settings before proceeding.
+3. Open **Technology**, select **TECCUT** and choose **Assign** on the matching row. Inspect the generated steps. The expected rough and trim offsets are **0.245, 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm**, in that order.
+4. Run **FORMALCHECK**. Inspect errors and warnings. Save the piece and run **GRAFICHECK**. Check the installed XY datum and travel, the approach from the hole and compensation outside the punch. Verify the 1 mm separation section, trimming sequence and support for release. CamCraft does not command a manual pause before the section cut.
